sketches: An n-vertex tournament is an n-chromatic oriented graph, so g(k) <= f(k) where f is the general oriented-graph function of Problem __00 and g its tournament restriction; the conjecture g(k) <= k^{4/3+o(1)} is the tournament instance of the same extremal question. Determining f resolves the tournament case up to the conjectured exponent.

source.name: Acyclic high-chromatic subgraph existence in tournaments
source.statement: What is the minimum integer $f\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(k}\right)$ such that every $f\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(k}\right)$-chromatic oriented graph has an acyclic $k$-chromatic subgraph?
source.context: Addario-Berry, Havet, Sales, Reed, and Thomassé observed that if a $k$-chromatic oriented graph has no directed cycle it contains every oriented tree of order $k$, and suggested that proving acyclic subgraphs of high chromatic number exist in $k$-chromatic oriented graphs could yield improved bounds towards Burr's conjecture. The trivial two-part partition gives $f(k)\leq k^{2}$, subsequently refined to $f(k)\leq k^{2}-2k+2$, but substantially improving this bound seems to require new ideas.

target.name: Acyclic subgraph chromatic number in tournaments
target.statement: Every $n$-vertex tournament has an acyclic subgraph with chromatic number at least $n^{3/4-o\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(1}\right)}$. That is, $g\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(k}\right)\leq k^{4/3+o\mathopen{}\mathclose{{}\left(1}\right)}$.
target.context: Having established $k^{4/3-o(1)}\leq g(k)\leq k^{9/5+o(1)}$, the authors suspect the lower bound is closer to the truth and propose this conjecture. The lower bound is achieved via a randomized projective-plane construction, and the authors also wonder whether a simpler explicit construction on $n=q^{2}$ vertices attains the same bound.

sketches: A digraph H admits constants c_epsilon for every epsilon > 0 (Question __02) exactly when the directed chromatic threshold epsilon_H of Question __03 equals 0. Hence determining epsilon_H for all H resolves which H satisfy __02.

source.name: Directed chromatic threshold for digraph subgraphs
source.statement: For a fixed digraph $H$, what is the minimum value $\varepsilon_{H}\geq 0$ such that there exists a constant $c\geq 1$ such that every digraph $D$ without loops or parallel arcs with $\chi(D)\geq c$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon_{H}|V(D)|$ contains $H$ as a subdigraph?
source.context: The quantity $\varepsilon_H$ provides a directed analogue of the chromatic threshold studied for undirected graphs. Theorem 1.3 may be interpreted as characterizing the orientations of cycles for which the directed chromatic threshold $\varepsilon_H$ equals zero. The authors also suggest studying variants where high chromatic number is replaced by high dichromatic number.

target.name: Digraph H-subgraph via χ and out-degree
target.statement: For which fixed digraphs $H$ does there exist a constant $c_{\varepsilon}\geq 1$ for all $\varepsilon>0$ such that every digraph $D$ without loops or parallel arcs with $\chi(D)\geq c_{\varepsilon}$ and minimum out-degree at least $\varepsilon|V(D)|$ contains $H$ as a subdigraph?
target.context: This is a more general version of Question 1.2, replacing cycle orientations by arbitrary fixed digraphs $H$. Theorem 1.3 characterizes the orientations of cycles for which this question is answered affirmatively. The authors also note that all subdigraphs of directed complete bipartite digraphs (with uniform arc orientation between parts) give an affirmative answer via a Ramsey-type argument.

sketches: Characterizing the minimal families of tournaments H1,...,Hk with {K-vec2, K-digon2, H1,...,Hk} heroic is the restriction of the general heroic-set characterization Problem 1.2 to sets consisting of the single arc, the digon, and tournaments; the general characterization answers it.

source.name: Heroic sets for bounded dichromatic number
source.statement: What are the finite sets $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs for which the class $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ has bounded dichromatic number?
source.context: This is the central problem of the paper, extending the Gyárfás-Sumner interrogation to directed graphs via the dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}$. A finite set $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs is called heroic if $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ has bounded dichromatic number. The paper focuses primarily on characterizing heroic sets of size three.

target.name: Minimal heroic tournament set classification
target.statement: Characterize all finite and minimal families $\mathcal{H} = \{H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k\}$ of tournaments such that $\{\overrightarrow{K_2}, \overleftrightarrow{K_2}, H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k\}$ is a heroic set.
target.context: Theorem 2.2 of Berger et al. [4] characterizes minimal heroic sets of this form with $|\mathcal{H}|=1$ (i.e., single-hero extensions). The authors note that a minimal heroic subset of order 2 or more cannot contain a hero tournament, making the general classification a natural open direction.

sketches: Take m=2 in the multicolour statement: a 2-colouring of E(K_n) encodes a graph G and its complement, 'k vertices coloured according to χ' is an induced copy of the k-vertex graph H encoded by χ, and 'n^ε vertices using at most 1 colour' is a clique or stable set of size n^ε. Quantifying over all 2-colourings χ of E(K_k) recovers exactly the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.

Take m=2 colours (edge/non-edge of a fixed H on k vertices): the multicolour conjecture then yields either k vertices coloured according to H (an induced copy of H) or n^eps vertices using at most one colour (a clique or independent set). So the classical Erdos-Hajnal conjecture is the m=2 instance.

Take m=2 and colour E(K_k) by edges/non-edges of H: a 2-colouring of E(K_n) is a graph, k vertices coloured per chi form an induced H, and n^eps vertices using at most one colour form a clique or independent set - exactly Erdos-Hajnal for H.

source.name: Multicolour Erdős--Hajnal Conjecture
source.statement: Conjecture For every fixed $ k\geq2 $ and fixed colouring $ \chi $ of $ E(K_k) $ with $ m $ colours, there exists $ \varepsilon>0 $ such that every colouring of the edges of $ K_n $ contains either $ k $ vertices whose edges are coloured according to $ \chi $ or $ n^\varepsilon $ vertices whose edges are coloured with at most $ m-1 $ colours.

target.name: The Erdös-Hajnal Conjecture
target.statement: Conjecture For every fixed graph $ H $ , there exists a constant $ \delta(H) $ , so that every graph $ G $ without an induced subgraph isomorphic to $ H $ contains either a clique or an independent set of size $ |V(G)|^{\delta(H)} $ .
target.context: There are numerous interesting classes of graphs which are based upon forbidding one or more induced subgraphs. For instance: chordal graphs , split graphs , and claw-free graphs. Numerous other natural classes of graphs have been proved to have such characterizations, most famously perfect graphs , but also line graphs and comparability graphs . All of these classes are very well structured (far from random) and their members all either have large cliques or independent sets. On the flip side of this are random graphs . It is well known that a random graph on $ n $ vertices has both clique and independence number highly concentrated around $ 2 \log_2 n $ . The Erdos-Hajnal conjecture suggests a fundamental separation between these two worlds in terms of independence/clique sizes. Erdös and Hajnal proved that this conjecture is true for the recursive class of graphs $ {\mathcal C} $ defined as follows. The one vertex graph is in $ {\mathcal C} $ , and if $ G_1 $ and $ G_2 $ lie in $ {\mathcal C} $ , then the disjoint union of $ G_1 $ and $ G_2 $ lies in $ {\mathcal C} $ , as does the graph obtained from the disjoint union by adding an edge between $ v_1 $ and $ v_2 $ for every $ v_1 \in V(G_1) $ and $ v_2 \in V(G_2) $ .
